features.name: negation_word_density_oc
features.definition: What proportion of all words across the counter-argument comments are negation words (not, no, never, nothing, etc.)?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments with json.loads; if missing/malformed return null. If list empty or total word count is 0 return null. Lowercase each comment; tokenize words with re.findall(r"[a-z]+(?:'[a-z]+)?", text). Negation tokens: the set {not, no, never, nothing, none, nobody, nowhere, neither, nor, cannot, without} plus any token ending in "n't" (e.g. don't, isn't, can't, won't). Value = total negation tokens across all comments / total word tokens across all comments (pooled over comments, in [0,1]). Raw mechanical count; no semantic filtering, so quoted text and any outcome announcements in comments are included.

h0: negation_word_density_oc has no association with the probability that the OP changed their view (delta).
h1: Higher negation_word_density_oc is associated with a lower probability that the OP changed their view.
note: Persuasiveness is operationalized as the dataset outcome delta (OP view change); association only, not causal. Negation lexicon is an operational assumption (the hypothesis gives "not, no, never, nothing, etc."). Density is pooled across all OC_comments; comments are unordered with unknown timing. Raw text may contain quotations of others and view-change/delta announcements; these are not excluded. Rows with no comments get null.
